Living in Switzerland ruined America For Me

Reading this reminded me when I lived in Switzerland and moved back. The reverse cultural shock was amazing. I had gotten used to how things worked in Switzerland, I totally forgot what daily life was like in America. I had taken public transportation being on time for granted, I enjoyed when I was on vacation no one would call me, and the food. The quality of food in Switzerland is comparable to America's Organic or local sourced. It was nice going to the grocery every other day for dinner for that night. I wasted less food and only bought what I was using that night.

Now I want to go back. Thanks, article! You ruined America tonight for me too. I had fully repressed those memories and began being an over-consumer again.
As an European looks like in America everyone works against you while in Europe we work together.

So I enjoy the Beatles' later stuff, but I was not a big fan of their early works. I always thought they sounded like a "damn cover band" in their early years. But lately I got hold of their Number Ones album and listening to it gave me a better perspective of their progression as artists.

So over the next few weeks, I am going to use this thread to go through their first six studio albums and give my impressions of what I think they did well, what I didn't like, and how I see the Beatles changing. I'll steer clear of existing analysis until after I finish each album. So here we go ... In Which I Listen to the Beatles.
I listen to the Beatles early studio albums

Please Please Me - their first studio album.

1 Kicking off with 'I Saw Her Standing There,' we've got a rocking number that showcases why they were so good in the clubs. You can put yourself in a basement club atmosphere with George's guitar going and slightly raw vocals. Throw in the track of hand claps and you've got yourself something.

2 'Misery' is a lost my girl kind of song. Simple performance with a piano kicked in there, and it has that Beatles' sound of a late 50s-early 60s race record. For me it kind of falls flat; I think it could have done with a little more arrangement.

3, 4, 5 'Chains,' 'Anna' and 'Boys' show the Beatles influence and appreciation of 60s American black music groups. These covers are all well performed, but compared to the original I think 'Anna' is not as good. It comes off less race record and more Everly brothers, not Beatles. The other two are fun, and Boys is rocking and raw - the kind of song you would love to hear live for the energy. Plus you get to hear George singing 'Chains,' so that's a plus.

6 'Ask Me Why,' another Lennon (mostly)-McCartney composition, is a high school dance type of song to me. I can see the couples on the floor with the chaperones watching for naughty stuff; it's got that turn of the decade sound. It's a well performed change-up and I enjoy George's guitar work here.

7 The title 'Please Please Me' opens with some harmonica and has me head bopping while they do their early Beatles thing. Energetic music, simple lyrics with a hint of dirty in the title (O.o) and a bridge thrown in lyrically. Nice way to close out side 1.

8 'Love Me Do,' their US number one hit, opens side 2. Up-tempo, harmonica and tambourine, catchy lyrics (if repetitive, but written by a teenager, so hey) that you can't help but sing along or hum. Good open to this side.

9 The Beatles write a love letter in 'P.S. I Love You.' Nice harmonies and a kind of haunting vocal sound. Just hit me it sounds like a voice-over of a letter being read. Not a bad song, it works for them and the time period.

10 Back to the dance floor or jukebox with 'Baby It's You.' They say you cheat, but I love you, see how true of a guy I am. The backing sha-la-las are fun, and it's a solid performance of a slow-dance teen tune.

11 George is back, singing John's 'Do you Want to Know a Secret' which is a dun little 2-minute diversion. Not the most powerful vocals, but the arrangement is simple and low-key, and the track with the sticks toward the end comes in clear and just adds a pop.

12 Paul is the balladeer in 'A Taste of Honey,' a song from a Broadway play of the same name. I hate this song. It kills the whole flow of the album for me. So much better as instrumental from Herb Alpert.

13 'There's a Place' brings me back on track. Harmonies, harmonica, good beat and slightly deeper lyrics than the standard love you baby music.

14 Close the place down with 'Twist and Shout.' Finding out John had a cold and sore throat makes the raw vocals that much more 'huh' for me. This is an energetic cover from the Beatles, and if it weren't for the fact that I wanted Ferris Bueller to die, I might have had more love for this song in my earlier years.

Overall this was a damn good first studio album. Original songs were good and the band's love of American black musical acts are apparent. This is a performance band's performance in a studio, not something over-arranged and over-produced. Outside of a couple missteps in my eyes, I really enjoy this album. Yay Beatles!
